items.titleEn: Hara, where Fuji fills the sky
items.bodyEn: Hara, the thirteenth post town, was a small, flat village between the Ukishima marsh and the sea, with one of the finest views of Fuji on the road. Hiroshige made the mountain so tall here that its summit breaks through the top border of the print, while two women travellers and a porter walk past cranes feeding in the marsh.
items.sourceNote: Hiroshige, Hara: Mount Fuji in the Morning (Hōeidō Tōkaidō, 1833–34)

items.bodyEn: Hara's most famous native was Hakuin Ekaku, born here in 1686, who revived Rinzai Zen from his small temple Shōin-ji and devised the kōan of the sound of one hand clapping. An Edo-period verse ran: Suruga has two things too fine for it, the mountain of Fuji and Hakuin of Hara. He died at Shōin-ji in 1769.
items.ja: {駿河|するが}には{過|す}ぎたるものが{二|ふた}つあり{富士|ふじ}のお{山|やま}に{原|はら}の{白隠|はくいん}
items.kana: するがにはすぎたるものがふたつありふじのおやまにはらのはくいん

items.bodyEn: The station's name, 原, now means a plain or field, but the character began as 泉, a spring, under 厂, a cliff: water welling out at the foot of a rock face, hence source. When 原 drifted toward plain and origin, scribes added water on the left to make 源, the kanji still used for the source of a river.
items.sourceNote: Shuowen Jiezi, entry 原 (泉 under 厂); Kangxi Dictionary

items.bodyEn: 〜たことがある says that something is part of your life experience: I have climbed Fuji, I have eaten natto. It does not report a recent event, so it sounds odd about yesterday or this morning; there the plain past is enough. Use it for things that happened some time ago, or that you have only done once or twice.
items.ja: {富士山|ふじさん}に{登|のぼ}ったことがある。
items.kana: ふじさんにのぼったことがある。
